# PART 1 – The repository {#part-1-the-repository .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 1
:::

::: notes
Part one turns the folder of your workspace into a git repository. Until now the workspace has been a plain folder, deliberately, so that nobody had to learn git in the middle of the workshop. Git records the history of a folder as a sequence of deliberate snapshots, each with a date, an author and a sentence saying why it was taken. In this case the repository also has to keep out what the licence of GESIS forbids sharing. The first snapshot that it records will be your preregistration, as you declared it, before a word of the report is written.
:::

## Git in Positron {#git-in-positron .smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.small}
**The Source Control view** (Ctrl+Shift+G) holds the three places of git:

- **Changes** – the working directory, every file whose changes are not yet staged
- **Staged Changes** – the staging area, the changes gathered for the next commit
- **Graph** – the repository, one commit to a line, newest first
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.small}
**The loop**, one change at a time:

1. Edit a file and save it
2. Stage it with the plus sign on its row, or every file with the plus sign on the header of Changes
3. Write a message in the box above the lists, saying what the change does
4. Press Commit, or Ctrl+Enter in the box
:::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment .small}
Once on each machine, in a terminal (**Terminal → New Terminal**), git needs your name and email address for every commit: `git config --global user.name "Your Name"` and `git config --global user.email "you@example.com"`.
:::

::: {.src}
Git and GitHub for reproducible research, section 2, on the AR4DS site: codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html
:::

::: notes
Positron does the work of git in its Source Control view, which opens from the Activity Bar or with control shift G. The view holds the three places that git keeps. Changes is your working directory: every file that you have changed and not yet staged. Staged Changes is the holding area for the next snapshot. And the Graph at the foot of the view is the repository itself, one commit to a line. The loop is always the same: edit and save, stage what belongs together with the plus sign, write a message that says what the change does, and commit. The letter beside each file says what happened to it: U for a file that git does not track yet, A for added, M for modified. [advance] Git stamps every commit with a name and an email address, so set them once on each machine, in a terminal.
:::

## What stays out of the repository {#what-stays-out-of-the-repository .smaller}

::: {.small}
- The `.gitignore` of the workspace already names what git must not track: `/data_private/`, which holds the respondent file and everything built from it; `/_site/` and `/.quarto/`, the rendered report and the working files of Quarto; and `.class-tag`, your tag on the class chart
- In Positron the Explorer shows each ignored file in a paler grey, and the list of changes in the Source Control view leaves such files out
- The `.dta` files from GESIS belong in a folder outside the workspace. The `.gitignore` does not name them, so a file left inside the folder would be staged with everything else
- The report works on the aggregate files in `data/`. A chunk that read the respondent file would write its output into `_freeze/`, which git tracks
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
A file that is committed and pushed stays in the history of the repository even after it is deleted. Read the list under **Changes** before the first commit: nothing from `data_private/` and no `.dta` file may appear in it.
:::

::: {.src}
The `.gitignore` and the README of the workspace; Git and GitHub for reproducible research, section 4.
:::

::: notes
Before the first commit, decide what the repository must never hold, because its history is permanent. The workspace has done most of that for you. Its gitignore file names the private folder, which holds the respondent file that you built this morning and everything built from it, then the rendered site and the working files of Quarto, and your tag for the class chart. Positron shows such files in a paler grey and leaves them out of the list of changes. Two gaps remain, and closing them is up to you. The Eurobarometer files themselves belong outside the workspace, and the gitignore does not name them, so a file left inside the folder would be committed with everything else. And the report should stay on the aggregate files, because the frozen results of every chunk are tracked, and a chunk that read the respondent file would carry its output into the repository. [advance] So read the list under Changes before you commit.
:::

## Hands-on 1 – The first commit {#hands-on-1-the-first-commit .smaller}

::: {.small}
1. Open the folder of your workspace, `replication-lab-main`, with **File → Open Folder…**, and check the preregistration block of Task 5, the chunk labelled `prereg` in `index.qmd`: one choice on each `my_` line, and fields 1 and 4 completed. If you declared in the browser lab, copy the block from your notes first, exactly as you declared it
2. Once on this machine, set your name and email address with `git config --global`
3. In Source Control, press **Initialize Repository**. The files of the workspace appear under Changes, marked U: read the list, and check that it holds no `.dta` file and nothing from `data_private/`
4. Stage all the changes with **Stage All Changes**, the plus sign on the header of Changes, write a message such as `Add the workspace with the analysis declared in Task 5`, and commit
5. Hold the pointer over the commit in the Graph: its author, its date and time, and the short form of its identifier
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
This commit is the declaration. Everything that you write from now on comes after it in the history.
:::

::: notes
Your turn. Open the folder of your workspace, the one that you used yesterday, and look at the preregistration block of Task 5 before you do anything else: every my line should hold your choice, and the two dotted lines, the claim in your own words and the sentence from your causal graph, should be filled in. If they are not, fill them in now, from your notes of yesterday, and only then go on. If you declared in the browser lab, copy the block that you saved in your notes into the report first, exactly as you declared it. Set your name and email address in a terminal if this machine has never had them. Then press Initialize Repository, read the list of changes for anything from GESIS, stage everything, and commit with a message that says what the commit holds. [state the time] [advance] That commit is your declaration, and everything that follows this afternoon will sit after it in the history.
:::
